gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each candidate NAS costs to run as a 24/7 music server. Using the makers' own access and hibernation wattages at the EIA's August 2026 US residential rate of 18.16¢/kWh, with 4 h/day of drive access and 20 h/day hibernated, that comes to about $8/yr for the UGREEN DH2300, $11/yr for the DXP2800, $13/yr for the Synology DS225+, $23/yr for the Asustor AS5402T and $32/yr for the QNAP TS-264. The TS-264 draws more with its disks asleep (18.3 W) than the DXP2800 does while reading (16.38 W).
standout_why: I compared against the three pages ChatGPT cited: navidrome.org/docs/overview (only says 'very low resource usage' and Raspberry Pi Zero, no numbers), ai.ugreen.com's Navidrome Docker guide (prices only, no wattage) and support.plex.tv's Sonic Analysis article (x86-only and 'hours or multiple days', no power or CPU figures). The uncited Plex hardware pages and the QNAP Plex page in the results are about transcoding. None gives power draw or running cost for a NAS that is always on. UGREEN's own blog does a yearly-cost sum for the DXP2800, but that page was not among ChatGPT's results and covers no rival brands.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's top pick, the DXP2800: it is the cheapest x86 box to run that can do Plexamp Sonic Analysis ($11.29/yr), and $1.27/yr cheaper than the DS225+. It weakens the TS-264, which costs about $20.67/yr more than the DXP2800 to run, or about $103 over 5 years, on top of a higher price. For a Navidrome-only shopper, the ARM DH2300 is cheapest overall: $239.99 plus about $40 of power over 5 years, against $389.99 plus about $56 for the DXP2800. It can't run Plex's Sonic Analysis.
